tier_justification: Standard soundness of k-induction (Sheeran, Singh and Stålmarck 2000), restated in this package's depth convention, which is that of Jovanović and Dutertre 2016 (Definition II.2). Soundness of k-induction encodings was mechanized earlier in Coq (Ishii and Fujii 2020).
plain_claim: For every transition system (finite or infinite, with or without dead-end states) and every depth k: if every path from an initial state with at most k states stays in P (Base k: all path lengths below k are checked, not only the longest) and every path of k+1 states whose first k states satisfy P ends in P (Step k), then every reachable state satisfies P.

hypotheses.name: hbase : Base I T P k
hypotheses.purpose: Establishes P on every state reachable in fewer than k transitions, which the step assumes without proof (vacuous at k = 0, where Step 0 alone says P holds everywhere).

hypotheses.name: hstep : Step T P k
hypotheses.purpose: Propagates P beyond the depth covered by the base.

nonvacuity_witness: TwoInd (states Fin 3, 0 initial with a self-loop, unreachable edge 1 -> 2, P excludes 2) at depth k = 2.
non_claims: Does not say Base k and Step k ever hold together for a given invariant: plain k-induction can fail at every depth even on a finite system (plain-kind-incomplete-every-depth).
The base depth matters: Base (k-1) together with Step k is not sound (kind_sound_base_depth_tight, k = 2). Literature depth indices differ by one in various ways; translate before comparing.

Base k checks every prefix length j < k, not only paths with exactly k-1 transitions. A base check over paths of exact length k-1 only (a single fixed-length unrolling, as in SAT encodings that assume a total transition relation) is unsound when some states have no successor (exact_length_base_unsound_without_totality); it is equivalent to Base k when every state has a successor (exact-length-base-needs-totality).
At k = 0, Base 0 is vacuous (it covers no state, not even the initial ones) and Step 0 says that P holds in every state.

Step quantifies over all paths, including paths through unreachable states and paths that revisit initial states. Of the variants that add constraints to the step, only the simple-path constraint is modelled (kind-simple-sound). A 'no initial state after position 0' constraint on the step (Eén and Sörensson note that intermediate states of a shortest counterexample are not initial) and the separate termination check of Sheeran et al. (which applies that constraint to loop-free paths from initial states) are not modelled.

Toy model: an abstract transition system (a state type in any universe, an initial-state predicate, and a transition relation that need not be total) and a state property; paths are explicit finite state sequences. No symbolic encoding, SAT/SMT solving, incremental algorithms, input variables, fairness, or liveness. These theorems neither establish nor refute the corresponding claims about SAT/SMT-based k-induction engines, bounded model checkers, or IC3/PDR implementations. Transfer to a real model checker is a separate modelling argument this package does not provide.

Stålmarck, 'Checking Safety Properties Using Induction and a SAT-Solver', FMCAD 2000, LNCS 1954, pp. 127-144 (pages as on the publisher's page; the dblp record conf/fmcad/SheeranSS00 lists pp. 108-125), doi:10.1007/3-540-40922-X_8. Assumes that every state has a successor (Section 2.2). Defines a path of length n as n transitions and loopFree paths (pairwise distinct states). Footnote 3 (Section II): 'If P is k-inductive then P ∧ ◦P ∧ ◦◦P ∧ ... ∧ ◦◦···◦P [k-1 operators] is inductive, where ◦ stands for "next state"'; reading ◦ as 'in every successor state', this conjunction is FutureSafe T P (k-1). The footnote has no proof and concerns plain (not simple-path) k-induction. tier_justification: Standard graph fact: every state reachable from an initial state is reachable from an initial state along a simple path that is no longer. A reduction of safety to loop-free paths was mechanized in Coq by Ishii and Fujii 2020 (their Lemma 1).
plain_claim: For every transition system, if a state s is reachable from an initial state in m transitions, then s is reachable from an initial state along a simple path (pairwise distinct states) with at most m transitions.
unfolded: ReachIn I T m s → ∃ m' ≤ m, ∃ π, I (π 0) ∧ IsPath T m' π ∧ IsSimple m' π ∧ π m' = s

hypotheses.name: h : ReachIn I T m s
hypotheses.purpose: The state must be reachable at all.

nonvacuity_witness: In SelfLoop, the initial state 0 is reached in 3 transitions around its self-loop (a non-simple path).

tier_justification: Folklore property of k-induction (success persists at larger depths), made explicit for both the plain and the simple-path step.
plain_claim: For every transition system and depths k <= k': if Base k and Step k hold then Base k' and Step k' hold; Step k alone implies Step k'; and SimpleStep k alone implies SimpleStep k'.
unfolded: Base I T P k → Step T P k → k ≤ k' → Base I T P k' ∧ Step T P k';   Step T P k → k ≤ k' → Step T P k';   SimpleStep T P k → k ≤ k' → SimpleStep T P k'

hypotheses.name: hb : Base I T P k (kind_success_mono)
hypotheses.purpose: Needed for Base k' (soundness turns Base k ∧ Step k into invariance, which gives every base check).

hypotheses.name: hs : Step T P k (kind_success_mono)
hypotheses.purpose: Needed for each conjunct separately: without it Base k' can fail (OneEdge), and even for an invariant P, Step k' can fail (SelfLoop).

hypotheses.name: hk : k ≤ k' (kind_success_mono)
hypotheses.purpose: Monotonicity is upward only.

hypotheses.name: h : Step T P k (Step.mono)
hypotheses.purpose: The step must hold at the smaller depth.

hypotheses.name: hk : k ≤ k' (Step.mono)
hypotheses.purpose: Step is not antitone: TwoInd passes Step 2 but not Step 1.

hypotheses.name: h : SimpleStep T P k (SimpleStep.mono)
hypotheses.purpose: The simple-path step must hold at the smaller depth.

hypotheses.name: hk : k ≤ k' (SimpleStep.mono)
hypotheses.purpose: SimpleStep is not antitone: SelfLoop passes SimpleStep 2 but not SimpleStep 1.

nonvacuity_witness: TwoInd with k = 2, k' = 3 (Base 2, Step 2); SelfLoop with k = 2, k' = 3 for SimpleStep (where Step 2 fails).
non_claims: Base alone is antitone, not monotone, in the depth: Base (k+1) implies Base k, not conversely.
Monotonicity means iterating k upward never loses a success; it gives no bound on the first successful depth.

Monotonicity of success is proved for plain k-induction (Base k ∧ Step k); for the simple-path variant only the step check is shown monotone (SimpleStep.mono), which together with soundness gives the same conclusion.

plain_claim: For every k there is a finite system, Ladder k (states Fin (k+2); initial state 0 with a self-loop; an unreachable chain 1 -> 2 -> ... -> k+1; P excludes k+1), whose property P is invariant and passes Base (k+1) and Step (k+1), while the step fails at every depth j <= k even when restricted to simple paths (SimpleStep j fails, hence Step j fails).
unfolded: ∀ k, Invariant (Ladder.I k) (Ladder.T k) (Ladder.P k) ∧ Base … (k+1) ∧ Step … (k+1) ∧ ∀ j ≤ k, ¬ SimpleStep (Ladder.T k) (Ladder.P k) j
nonvacuity_witness: The statement is a parametric family of concrete systems.
non_claims: Fixed-depth incompleteness applies to the simple-path step as well as to the plain step: the witness chain 1 -> ... -> k+1 in Ladder k is already simple. Incremental formulations that check every length up to k (as k grows) do not need totality; Base in this package is of that kind.
Making a relation total by adding self-loops to dead ends changes the system; whether that preserves the property of interest is a separate question not addressed here.
